items.title: Cosimo Matassa Interview, 1994-01-15
items.q: Ralph Pate was the guy's name. He had run a big pressing plant... I represented an opportunity for him too. And so that's how we got together.

ctx.x: political ambitions are concerned. Okay, so we're back on real we're on real four now with Cosmo Matassa, hoping that the squeaking birds don't chirp anymore. I don't hear them. And so it's January 15, 1994, real four. All right, so yeah, we were talking about getting in Dover.

Do you remember who ran your pressing plan? Yeah, yeah. Ralph Pate was the guy's name. He had run a big pressing plant in in Memphis for years and had some other experience. And he was working for how how he got to to to to work for me was he was working for the guy that owned that pressing plant named Williams. And Williams had a lot of money in oil wells and things like that. And when when Williams shut down the pressing plant, Peyton went to work for him in his oil business because he understood that…
That you needed to produce 40 and 50,000 a day.
